blocks.text: CyAICodex keeps reusable instructions (Skills) and image references in one local library. Edit them yourself, ask the integrated assistant for help, and let connected AI clients consult the same published resources.

nodes.title: CyAICodex on Windows
nodes.text: Local library, MCP server and notification-area icon.

nodes.title: Your AI clients
nodes.text: Codex, Claude, OpenCode or another MCP client.

blocks.text: The browser is the interface. The Windows process runs the server. Closing the browser tab leaves the server available while the PC is awake. External AI clients connect through MCP; the integrated assistant is a separate way to draft content.

This manual, screenshots and diagrams are bundled with the application. Reading them needs no Internet, AI account or API key. External providers, GitHub downloads and online references require their respective services.
Use the chapter list or search, which ignores accents. The manual follows the interface language; English is the default and French is available. Screenshots contain sample data.

items: Run the Windows installer and keep _internal next to CyAICodex.exe. Python is not required for the installed version.
Open CyAICodex from Start, your shortcut or the green CY book icon in the Windows notification area.
In Library, open a bundled GitHub checklist or click New skill. Write a title, summary and instructions; choose a scope and Published when ready.
In Connections > Configure and test, choose your client and access settings, then configure and test. Reconnect the MCP server in the client or restart that client.
Ask the AI to call get_context, search_skills and get_skill. A published result in the intended scope confirms it can read the library.

blocks.text: The library works manually before connecting any AI. English and French starter checklists are added once. Updates preserve your adaptations.

blocks.caption: Library overview: search, scope filters and published Skills.

items: Open Library > New skill, or click an existing card to edit it.
Use a specific title and summary explaining when the skill applies. Write prerequisites, ordered actions, expected result and checks in The skill.
Choose a category and comma-separated tags. Tags and summary help search; keep secrets and personal credentials out of reusable instructions.
Choose Global, Project type or Specific project, selecting the group where needed. Set Published, Draft or Archived, then save.

rows: What the skill does and when to consult it.
Text with Markdown headings, steps and checklists.
Which project contexts may access the published skill.
Published: visible through MCP. Draft / Archived: kept for you, excluded from MCP.

blocks.text: To retire a skill, choose Archived and save. A draft can be refined before publishing. Changing interface language never translates or rewrites your content.
Library Skills are instruction records. They are not automatically created or installed as native SKILL.md packages in other software.

blocks.caption: Editor: classification, scope, instructions and publication settings.

items: Enter a few meaningful words in Library search: title fragments, tags or terms from the summary/content.
Combine search with category, context and status filters. Toggle Include global skills when working within a project.
Browse with Previous / Next. Clear text and category filters if an expected record is missing.

blocks.text: SQLite full-text search normalizes accents, matches word prefixes and ranks titles, summaries and tags highly. Several words narrow results. This is not semantic/vector similarity search.
The interface can list drafts and archives via the status filter. MCP always returns published resources in the connection’s scope, with short excerpts; get_skill retrieves the complete record.
An empty AI search can reflect scope, publication state or search terms. Check get_context before assuming the server is disconnected.

items: Open an existing Skill and expand Version history.
Choose Resume this version to load an earlier snapshot. Review the fields before saving.
Save to create a new current version. Loading an old snapshot does not erase later history.

blocks.text: Each saved edit records a revision. If another client changed the record since you opened it, saving returns a conflict instead of overwriting that edit. Reload the latest version, compare your changes, then save deliberately.

MCP writers send expected_version from get_skill or get_image. A conflict requires reading again. Image-description history does not restore older image pixels; import visual variants as separate resources.

items: In Projects & types, create a type such as Web application, then a project linked to it.
Assign each Skill/image to Global, that type or that specific project.
In Connections, choose each AI’s project or type context and whether global resources are included.

nodes.title: Global skills
nodes.text: Only when Include global is enabled.

blocks.text: A project connection combines that project, its type and optionally globals. A type-only connection sees that type and optionally globals. Without project/type, only globals can be visible when included. Other projects stay outside scope.
Each connection has its own context. Multiple clients can work on different projects simultaneously. Write access covers every accessible resource, including globals when included.

blocks.caption: A sample project associated with a project type.

items: Open Image resources > Import an image and select a still PNG, JPEG or WebP.
Describe it, specifying what to preserve, changes to avoid, allowed usage and source. Add category, tags, scope and status.
Save and inspect transparency on the preview checkerboard. Download original returns the imported file.
Edit instructions on the existing resource; import a visual variant as a new resource. Use with assistant selects the reference for the next request.

rows: 8192 pixels per side and 25 million pixels maximum.
Stored unchanged with SHA-256, dimensions and format metadata.

blocks.text: Published images follow the same context/write rules as Skills. get_image supplies metadata and the local original-file path for clients on this PC; view_image supplies a smaller preview. A PC file path is not a cloud download link.
CyAICodex stores references and instructions. It does not generate or edit image pixels. Do not replace the original with a screenshot of its preview.

topics.title: Connect Codex, Claude Desktop or OpenCode

items: Start CyAICodex and open Connections > Configure and test.
Choose token access, or existing local token-free access if deliberately enabled. Select scope, Include global and write rights where available.
On the target client’s card, click Configure and test. Recognized configurations are backed up; other servers are preserved. Invalid files and unrelated same-name entries are not overwritten.
Reconnect CyAICodex in the target client or restart that client. An open client may retain an older tool list.
Use Test only, then ask the AI itself for get_context, search_skills and get_skill to verify what it actually reads.

nodes.title: Client configured
nodes.text: The client has a CyAICodex entry.

blocks.text: The same CyAICodex.exe handles the interface and --mcp-stdio. Stdio clients can start the shared server on demand. Closing a client does not quit the independent tray server. A separate bridge executable is unnecessary.
Access to the library does not connect an assistant account. MCP setup and the integrated assistant’s provider login are separate tasks.

topics.title: Other clients and AI setup guides

items: Create a named connection in Connections with the required scope and rights.
Copy its generated configuration while the token is visible. Choose your client’s format and follow its MCP settings.
For Streamable HTTP, use the local /mcp address and Bearer token with the server running. For stdio, use the generated executable command and arguments.
Reconnect the client and run a real MCP test. A browser opening /mcp is not a protocol test.

blocks.text: Under Information to share with another AI, download an English or French Markdown guide and attach it to the conversation. A connected AI can call get_setup_guide(client, language). Claude Desktop and Claude Code are distinct clients; automatic setup covers Codex, Claude Desktop and OpenCode.

Local discovery uses /mcp-info and the guide /mcp-guide. Neither contains tokens or library content. Markdown describes the steps; a user or authorized capable agent still has to configure the client.

At the start of each task, call get_context, then search_skills and get_skill for applicable practices. Respect this connection’s scope. Create or update a skill only when I ask; use expected_version for updates.
A cloud AI cannot directly reach this PC’s localhost. Use a local client or compatible local execution environment; do not expose the server to the Internet as a shortcut.

rows: Read published in-scope resources; no creation or update.
Create/update accessible resources, globals included when enabled.
Let local processes use the configured scope and rights without a Bearer token.
Preselect writes for new token connections; existing ones do not change.

blocks.text: Change an existing connection’s write checkbox in Connections. Tokens are shown once at creation; only their hash is kept in the library. Revocation requires configuring new access. Never paste secrets into chats, screenshots or public support reports.

Settings > MCP permissions defines the token-free context, global inclusion and write rights. It does not remove project scope checks or separate administration protection. AI-client approval prompts are managed in that client, not by this toggle.

Local storage does not mean assistant requests stay local. Sending a message sends conversation and selected references to the chosen provider. Ollama or LM Studio can run locally; cloud providers receive requests under their own policies.

items: In Connections or Settings, verify the local client or save the provider API credentials. Use its native login when offered.
In Assistant, select provider and model, or leave the model blank where the provider supports a default.
Optionally select a Skill and an image reference. Describe the reusable procedure or preservation instructions you want, then send.
Review the answer. Turn into a skill opens a draft editor: choose scope, category and status, then save. Answer text alone does not save a record.

blocks.text: The conversation and selected references are resent with the request. Clear the conversation to start again. The assistant tab is not a guaranteed resumable native provider session; save important work as a Skill or another document.
Image support depends on both adapter and model. Choose a vision-capable model. The assistant analyzes references and drafts text; it does not generate images.

Claude Desktop MCP access lets Claude read the library. To chat inside CyAICodex with a Claude account, use supported Claude Code access or a separate Anthropic API key. Consumer subscriptions are not API credentials.

Install the provider’s client or start its server first. Custom executable paths in Settings can override detection. Checking availability, loading model names and testing a response are distinct actions.

rows: Local Codex client; check account and sign in through Connections.
Local Claude Code client and native account login.
Local OpenCode with configured provider; model format provider/model.
Local server, default http://127.0.0.1:11434; install a model separately.
Separate API key and exact model identifier.
Separate Anthropic API key and exact model identifier.
Detected agy CLI and its signed-in account.
Detected cmdc / command-code CLI and account.
Detected codebuddy / cbc CLI and account.
OpenRouter API key and model identifier.

blocks.text: Additional connectors

items: In Settings > Additional connectors, save the client path or server address and credentials as applicable.
Check, then Load models where supported. Choose a returned model or enter a supported identifier.
Optionally Test a response. This sends a small control message, may consume quota, and does not send the library’s Skills.
Select the same provider/model in Assistant for your real request.

blocks.text: Model catalogs and account entitlements can change. Availability does not prove access to every model. These buttons do not install models. LM Studio requires a local HTTP address ending in /v1; Ollama also requires a local address.

Antigravity and Command Code use native plan modes and integrations; CyAICodex does not relay approval prompts. CodeBuddy disables tools in this adapter. Do not assume all CLI adapters have identical execution capabilities.

items: In Connections > Server availability, enable Start with Windows, or use the same setting in the tray menu.
On the next Windows sign-in, CyAICodex starts in the background without opening the browser. Reopen it from the tray icon.
To stop it, choose Quit and stop server in the tray. Clients lose access until the server starts again.

blocks.text: Startup occurs after user sign-in, not before login. The PC must be awake. Closing the browser does not stop the server; sleep and shutdown make it unavailable.
If a copied URL asks you to reopen from the icon, use the tray icon or application shortcut. It establishes the protected administration session. Do not share its temporary launch link.
Keep _internal next to the executable. The application and MCP use these installed components without unpacking a new Temp copy for every connection.

items: Choose English or Français in FR / EN, or Settings > App language.
The application reloads and saves the choice. Manual and tray menu follow it; the assistant is asked to reply in that language.
Navigate the manual with Tab and Enter. Diagrams have textual descriptions; screenshots have captions. Print this chapter opens your browser’s print dialog for the selected chapter.

blocks.text: Without a saved choice, English is used. Updates preserve French preferences. Skills, projects, categories, image descriptions and unknown provider messages are not translated automatically. The GitHub starter exists in both languages.
In the standalone manual, its EN / FR selector changes that view only, not your saved application preference.

nodes.text: JSON: Skills and classification to inspect or share.

nodes.title: Full backup
nodes.text: Stop CyAICodex and copy the entire data folder.

nodes.title: Restore
nodes.text: Stop, preserve current data, restore a complete backup.

blocks.text: Export library at the bottom of Library downloads skills.json: Skill records and classification without account keys or tokens. It is not a full backup of images, settings, credentials and history. This version has no general JSON import button.
Full backup

items: Quit and stop the tray server. Close/disconnect MCP clients so they do not restart it immediately.
Copy the entire %LOCALAPPDATA%\CyAICodex\data folder to your backup location. Portable/source copies use data beside the application unless --data-dir overrides it.
Keep originals, database and companion SQLite files together. Protect the backup: it can contain private instructions and connection information.

blocks.text: Restore

items: Stop the server and clients again. Keep the current data folder separately as a recovery copy.
Restore the complete backup to the intended data location and reopen CyAICodex.
Check representative Skills, image originals, history and connections.

blocks.text: DPAPI credentials are tied to the Windows account/profile that encrypted them. Another account/PC may require entering credentials again. Older libraries may use methodes.sqlite3; new ones use skills.sqlite3. Do not rename or merge open databases manually.

items: Open Settings > Updates and Check for updates.
For a private repository, enable local Git GitHub credentials or supply a repository token with Contents: read access. Public releases need no authentication.
If a newer stable version is offered, Download and install. The installer’s size and GitHub SHA-256 digest are checked before the wizard opens.
Complete the installer and its license screen. The server/connections stop temporarily. Reopen the app and reconnect clients afterwards.

blocks.text: Automatic checks, when enabled, run shortly after startup and every six hours. They do not install automatically. Drafts, prereleases, older versions and assets without a valid expected digest are not installed.
Portable migration

Quit the portable app, then run the installer with /LEGACYDATA="absolute path to data". It copies a consistent library and preserves the original. An existing destination library is not replaced. Recognized MCP entries are updated while other servers are kept; use Configure and test for manual repairs.

The normal install location is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\CyAICodex. Uninstall through Windows Apps or the installed uninstaller. The library in %LOCALAPPDATA%\CyAICodex\data is preserved. Uninstalling does not revoke external accounts or remove every AI client configuration.

rows: Start CyAICodex, check the tray and that the PC is awake. Default port 8765 may be occupied by another app.
Use the tray icon or shortcut to establish the administration session. Do not share launch links.
Reconnect MCP or restart the AI client, then Test only. Saved configuration is not proof the client reloaded.
Reconfigure the intended connection; do not paste tokens in support chats.
Check Published state, scope, Include global, search/category filters and get_context.
Reload and compare edits; do not overwrite blindly.
Check installation and native login, then set its executable path. Desktop and CLI can be separate.
Start Ollama and install a model separately, then Check and select it.
Check adapter/model vision support, file format and size limits.
Check local Git access or the limited repository token, network and release availability.
This is a user sign-in startup setting, not a pre-login system service.
Keep _internal intact and repair/reinstall the app; assets need no remote download.

blocks.text: The rotating log is cyaicodex.log in the application data folder. Installation writes installation.log beside that folder. Earlier releases may use methodes.log. Share only the relevant redacted error and app version, never the whole library, credentials or tokens.
Keep data and backups after startup/update failures. Diagnose first; do not delete your library to fix a connection issue.

rows: Read scope, global inclusion and write permissions.
Find published Skills and read full content/version.
Write when authorized; updates require expected_version.
Find images, read their rules and view a preview.
Add a local absolute file path or base64 image and its description.
Update rules with expected_version; original pixels remain intact.
Client setup guidance in English or French.

blocks.text: Legacy search_methods, get_method, create_method and update_method remain supported. skills://context and methodes://context expose scope. apply_skills is the current prompt; appliquer_methodes remains compatible.

Transport is Streamable HTTP on the local /mcp endpoint or the generated stdio command. Standard port: 8765. Source/CLI options include --port, --data-dir, --no-open, --headless, --mcp-stdio and --stop for deliberately managed custom instances.
MCP makes resources available, but cannot force a model to consult them. Put get_context → search_skills → get_skill in client instructions. Permissions and context always apply.

items: Read the English or French GitHub starter Skill and adapt it to your actual publication process.
Keep generally reusable rules global; use a project/type scope for specialized instructions. Publish after review.
Give the development AI a read-only connection with the right scope and global inclusion.
Before a commit/release, ask it to read the Skill, inspect the actual outgoing files/history and report privately.
After an improvement, explicitly request a proposed or saved revision. Give write access only to the intended connection, using the current version.

blocks.text: For a logo, use the same pattern: import the approved original, specify the CY mark and transparency to preserve, publish in scope, then have the AI read the rules and original before proposing a variant.
An example checklist is guidance, not a guarantee of leak-free publishing or blanket permission to push. Apply it to the actual files and release artifacts.

The manual version is shown above. Screenshots contain sample data; small label or color differences may occur across releases. No account credentials or personal libraries are used as examples.

Read Documentation in the app or /help separately while the local server runs. Search, illustrations and diagrams need no external resources. Offline still requires the local app/server; it does not mean cloud access to a powered-off PC.
For support, describe the version, client and failed step with a redacted error. Repository and releases are on GitHub and require Internet access.
